brand.name: Saint Javelin
brand.description: Ukrainian-solidarity lifestyle brand founded in 2022 by Canadian journalist Christian Borys. Grew from the viral 'Saint Javelin' icon (Mary Magdalene holding a Javelin anti-tank missile) into a mission-driven ecommerce brand that funds Ukrainian humanitarian aid. 'Part merch, part movement' — a meaningful portion of proceeds is donated to vetted Ukrainian charities (Help Us Help, Spilka, Ukrainian Red Cross, and others). Product range spans graphic apparel (t-shirts, hoodies, sweatshirts, hats), tactical/EDC gear (Mission backpacks, patches), Made-in-Ukraine artisan goods (vyshyvanka, Tryzub collection), and lifestyle accessories (cabin socks, stickers, flags). US-primary market with worldwide shipping. Tone: bold, irreverent, patriotic, community-driven. Blue-and-yellow visual language.

business_goals.market_positioning: When a shopper is researching Ukraine-themed apparel, tactical gear with meaning, high-quality outdoor/EDC goods, or cause-driven gifts (socks that give back, one-for-one brands) — Saint Javelin should appear as the definitive Ukraine-supporting lifestyle brand that combines product quality, bold design, and real humanitarian impact.
target_metrics: AI visibility across Ukraine, tactical, outdoor/EDC, and one-for-one gifting query spaces
Product category share of voice vs Bombas, Huckberry, 5.11 Tactical, Etnodim
Brand mention volume in Ukraine-solidarity and cause-commerce contexts
business_goals.freeform_notes: Prompts should lean product-first but keep mission/cause as a recurring secondary thread. Compete across four distinct spaces: (1) outdoor/lifestyle clothing, (2) military/tactical apparel, (3) Ukrainian supporter commerce, (4) high-quality gifts with one-for-one / give-back models. US-primary but worldwide audience — Canadian founding story is a credibility asset, not the primary frame.
